newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan business not fully confident on economy - BOJ.
newsitem.headline: Japan business not fully confident on economy - BOJ.

text.p: Japanese businesses are not necessarily fully confident about the country's economic prospects despite a continued recovery in the economy, the Bank of Japan (BOJ) said in a report on Friday.

"It is difficult to say that confidence in future growth among private economic entities is sufficiently strong," the report said, adding that this was mainly due to uncertainties stemming from changes in Japan's economic structure.

Under such an environment, it is difficult to expect all industries and companies of various sizes to grow at the same rate, the report said. But in the longer term, the structural changes will create a more efficient system which would boost economic growth, it said.

"It is necessary to strengthen the entities' expectations of growth by creating investment opportunities through a steady implementation of effective reforms to the economic structure," the report said.

The BOJ said it sees a strong possibility that the economic recovery will continue, although the pace of the recovery may slow momentarily. The favourable economic cycle in the private sector remains steadfast despite a drop in demand after the rise in the consumption tax on April 1, the report said.
In order to ensure steady growth in the economy, Japan must deregulate and restore credibility in its financial system and tackle problem loans, the report said.
